<!-- go-guitar-pro-capability-work:page-setup -->

Map legacy page header/footer templates and visibility to the supported GP8 BinaryStylesheet fields; retain physical geometry as a separate limit.

**Type:** implementation. **Priority:** P3. **Capability:** `page-setup`.
**Formats:** gp3, gp4, gp5, gp6, gp7, gp8. **Stages to assess:** import, model, export.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve the supported Title, Subtitle, Artist, Album, Words, Music, WordsAndMusic, Tabber and both Copyright template/visibility fields where present, using exact Header/* and Footer/* keys.
- [ ] Use pinned GP5 and GP8 header-footer fixtures with distinct non-default templates and visible/hidden fields. Verify public import/edit/export, exact stylesheet records and pinned consumer values.
- [ ] Define authority between the existing PageSetup templates/bitmask and any richer score-style representation. Split the legacy copyright lines deterministically and report ambiguous or lossy projection instead of discarding text.
- [ ] Retain explicit template absence/defaults; do not accidentally erase other supported stylesheet values. New alignment APIs are excluded; preserve the documented default alignment for projected legacy fields.

Any public API change must expose the authored value with a documented edit/reconciliation contract. Add a non-default public API regression and independent pinned-consumer export evidence. Preserve compatibility or explicitly document the change.

## Scope boundaries

- Physical dimensions, margins, score-size and page-number templates lack the required retaining GP8 oracle and remain separately reported.
- Alignment preservation is not silently promised by template support; existing non-default alignment must have an explicit disposition.

## Reproduction and evidence

Preserve the supported Title, Subtitle, Artist, Album, Words, Music, WordsAndMusic, Tabber and both Copyright template/visibility fields where present, using exact Header/* and Footer/* keys. See the linked investigation decision and review receipt for the confirmed baseline.

Use the named fixtures and non-default cases above. The linked investigation and review distinguish reproduced failures from source-backed implementation gaps.

- Repository [song.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1/song.go)
- Repository [gp8_builder.go](https://github.com/CaliLuke/go-guitar-pro/blob/30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1/gp8_builder.go)
- field: `Song.PageSetup`. Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.
- test: `TestConformancePageSetupImport`. Existing scoped evidence; not proof of all AlphaTab variants.

Oracle: AlphaTab 1.8.4, revision `022a45c8e42370f9e12e68949d11eada370da83d`. Audit baseline: `30436b08bf7f342ceda0d97c5ddd2c085db1b4f1`.

comments.body:
## Investigation complete — implementation-ready

**Disposition: header/footer templates and visibility are implementable; physical page geometry is not retained by the pinned GP8 model.**

Legacy 'guitarpro5/header-footer.gp5' and GP8 'guitarpro8/header-footer.gp' contain distinct non-default templates and visibility. GP8 stores the supported styles in BinaryStylesheet keys such as 'Header/Title', 'Header/drawTitle', alignment keys, and 'Footer/Copyright*'; pinned AlphaTab parses and writes them. Go's PageSetup has templates plus a bitmask but no alignment fields, so the bounded mapping is templates + visibility, with centered/default alignment unless a public alignment API is separately proposed. Split the two copyright lines deterministically and report lossy ambiguity.

Page width/height, margins, score-size proportion, and page-number template are read from GP5 by Go. The pinned legacy importer skips the seven numeric geometry values, and its GPIF writer emits empty HTML page-header/footer nodes. Although raw BinaryStylesheet contains additional page keys, pinned 'apply/writeForScore' does not map geometry. Keep those fields as explicit target limits until an independent GP8 oracle is defined.

Evidence: both pinned header/footer fixtures, 'readPageSetup', and 'BinaryStylesheet.writeForScore'. <!-- investigation-decision-ready-2026-09-10 -->

<!-- go-guitar-pro-capability-work:partial-capo -->

Acquire the finite evidence package needed to define a per-string capo mapping. Existing documentation establishes broad capo behavior; this task supplies actual source values, string-flag order and a retaining consumer result. It remains blocked on external authoring/consumer access and is excluded from autonomous implementation readiness.

**Type:** investigation. **Priority:** P3. **Capability:** `partial-capo`.
**Formats:** gp7, gp8. **Stages to assess:** import, model, export.

**Current direction:** Acquire the stated fixture/consumer package once. The next implementation task can then define the actual string mapping and public edit authority. Until it exists, keep this missing/target-limited and explicitly blocked on the two named inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Obtain an authorized GP7/GP8 fixture pair authored from the same minimal six-string score: no partial capo control and partial capo fret 3 on asymmetric named strings 1 and 4. Each string must have an identifiable open-string note. Record application version, string naming convention, file hashes and authored UI values.
- [ ] Add a combined-capo variant with whole capo 2 and partial capo 5, plus a partial-below-whole control. Reopen in the authoring application and record exact per-string state and output pitches; the verified documentation already states frets are absolute and a partial capo below the whole capo is ineffective.
- [ ] Extract and record exact GPIF PartialCapoFret and PartialCapoStringFlags fields. Change only one selected string in a controlled sibling file to establish bit/string order; do not infer order from tuning reversal.
- [ ] Run public Go ParseWithOptions and pinned AlphaTab on each fixture, recording retained facts and diagnostic paths. Record the independent Guitar Pro consumer facts separately because pinned AlphaTab has no retaining partial-capo field.
- [ ] Deliver fixtures and machine-readable receipts in the corpus/database with a narrow proposed mapping/API follow-up only if string ordering and a retaining consumer are proved. Otherwise record the exact missing input and keep the work excluded from ready_work; do not loop into another open-ended source review or promote support.

Deliver a reproducible decision with stage-specific evidence. Classify valid source loss, intentional format limits, derived values, malformed input, and oracle defects separately. Record follow-up implementation tickets for confirmed unresolved defects. Closing this investigation does not establish feature support.

## Scope boundaries

- No per-string API or pitch conversion before fixture facts exist.
- No tuning modification as a proxy; no AlphaTab upgrade; no claim that absence in AlphaTab validates values.

## Reproduction and evidence

Use Guitar Pro Track Inspector > Tuning > Partial Capo, following the linked official guide, to author the controlled corpus variants. After acquisition run node conformance/oracle.mjs testdata/gp8/partial-capo-asymmetric.gp; record their default/retained output as the pinned limit, not as an expected mapping. Extract GPIF with python3 -m zipfile -e INPUT.gp TEMP_DIRECTORY and compare only the named staff properties. Add a focused public Go ParseWithOptions regression that prints/asserts the corresponding source paths. Save hashes, exact wire values, authoring facts and outcomes in work-item/database receipts. No acquired file currently exists.

Use the source review and reproductions below as starting evidence. Add the fixture or inventory regression specified by the acceptance criteria; the lack of a saved probe is not evidence of support.

## Required external inputs

- **partial-capo-fixtures (missing)**: Authorized minimal GP7/GP8 control and nonzero partial-capo variants with asymmetric named strings and controlled single-string difference, including combined-capo cases.
  Acquisition: An existing licensed Guitar Pro user authors the stated variants through Track Inspector > Tuning > Partial Capo; use the official guide. If no authoring access is available, request this exact package from the repository owner and leave readiness blocked.
- **partial-capo-consumer-receipt (missing)**: Guitar Pro or another independently retaining consumer reopening the fixtures with application version, exact selected strings, fret values and per-string output pitches.

The complete pinned staff-property switch handles Tuning, chord collections and CapoFret; it has no PartialCapo reader or retained model mapping.

Fresh ZIP GPIF scan at reviewed commit: 376 containers parsed; 849 PartialCapoFret occurrences all 0; 849 PartialCapoStringFlags occurrences all zero; no non-default partial-capo source. 849 FretCount occurrences all 24.

## Investigation incomplete — needs evidence

> **Missing evidence:** A non-zero partial-capo fixture, confirmed string-flag bit order, and a consumer that retains the value are missing.

**Disposition: keep partial capo outside implementable parity until an oracle exists.**

GPIF Staff properties name 'PartialCapoFret' and 'PartialCapoStringFlags', so the container has a plausible representation. However the pinned AlphaTab parser does not retain them and its writer always emits fret 0 with all string flags clear. An exhaustive scan of the pinned GP archive corpus found no non-zero partial-capo instance, so there is no authorized source fixture or independent consumer result to establish semantics, string-bit order, or interaction with the existing whole-staff capo.

Do not infer partial capo from tuning or collapse it into the public single Capo value. The next AI should create an implementation task only after obtaining an authorized Guitar Pro fixture with a non-zero fret and asymmetric string flags plus a Guitar Pro (or other retaining consumer) oracle. Until then the justified scope decision is explicit unsupported/target-limit status. Dependency #43 remains the whole-capo owner.

Reviewed: pinned GPIF Staff parser/writer and full pinned fixture corpus. <!-- investigation-decision-ready-2026-09-10 -->

<!-- capability-review-next-steps-2026-09-10 -->

## Next steps after review

1. The next required artifact is a Guitar Pro fixture with a nonzero partial capo fret and asymmetric string flags, plus a consumer that retains those values.

2. Use it to establish flag/string order, pitch effects and interaction with whole-staff capo. Pinned AlphaTab currently discards the properties, so its default output cannot validate the semantics.

3. Once those facts are known, create a bounded mapping/API contract linked to #43. Until then keep the unsupported status explicit; do not infer the flags from tuning or collapse them into the whole-staff capo.

Before closing, check every acceptance criterion against the exact verified commit and record the decision/evidence in the canonical work item and SQLite inventory. Issue closure alone must not promote support.

<!-- capability-actionability-review-2026-09-11 -->

Replaced the open-ended investigation with a finite fixture-acquisition task. The named external inputs remain missing, so this item is excluded from `ready_work`.

Acquire the stated fixture/consumer package once. The next implementation task can then define the actual string mapping and public edit authority. Until it exists, keep this missing/target-limited and explicitly blocked on the two named inputs.

The body now records the exact inputs, missing assertions, scope boundaries, source references and acceptance checklist.

Keep the issue open until the fixture package and independent receipts satisfy its checklist. Mark each external input available only with its evidence reference; acquisition alone does not establish support.
